Investing can be daunting to new investors. It can take a long period of time before somebody feels comfortable with investing. This is a list of some do’s and don’ts of investing that should help reduce beginner mistakes.

**Do**

1. Use a virtual trading app – Dive into the investing world with a free virtual trading app. They are free and a great way to play the market without investing any of your own cash! I would highly recommend investing with a virtual trading app for a couple of weeks to months to get a feel of the stock market and figure out what stocks you may want to purchase. This is a great way to learn the stock market and make mistakes as it is not your own money. 2. Start early! - I cannot stress how important the concept of compounding is. If you do not know what compounding is check out my article on investing here. Investing as soon as possible gives your portfolio time to grow through the power of compounding and can ensure financial stability over a long period of time 3. Diversify – I’m sure you have heard many times the importance of diversification. Diversification is important so your portfolio is less risky. Buying stocks across multiple sectors that are not correlated can help stabilize your portfolio when a sector underperforms. 4. Start investing no matter how small it may be – Does not matter how small or large the investment is, getting into the stock market will help grow your earnings exponentially. 5. Research, a lot! – Perhaps the most important thing to do. Read articles about stocks, the financial markets, and what is currently happening in the world. Watch shows about stocks and what people are doing. When I now started to invest I did no research and this caused me to lose money. I bought stocks in a sector that was in decline due to my lack of research. Thankfully I was able to recover, and profit, as I read up on the market and watched CNBC (a channel dedicated just to the stock market with great advice) almost every day. 6. Invest in declining sectors – You may look at this and say I am crazy. But think about it, all sectors go up and all sectors go down at some point. Right now the energy sector (oil) is in a major crisis. Many of these companies are cheap and will probably go up in a few years. Take advantage of these declines. Disclaimer – I am not advising on buying oil company stocks, this is just an example of something that is happening in the world right now and presents a potential opportunity to generate wealth in the future. 7. Create core holdings – Invest in four or five core holdings. Think of these as the foundation that will support your future investments. These should be blue chip stocks that can stabilize your portfolio. These companies are not as volatile as most of the stock market and should help your portfolio survive any downturns. 8. Know your risk appetite – If you know you are somebody who can’t stand to see your portfolio in the red then do not invest in risky companies. Stick to companies with a Beta (the risk of the company) close to 1, or below, as they will not be as volatile. These stocks will obviously decline but your portfolio will decline less than investments in risky stocks. If you want the big gains, you will need to invest in speculative (high risk) companies, usually new start-ups, that you believe will be very successful. The greater the risk the greater the reward; however there will be a greater chance of potential losses. 9. Pay attention to trading fees – Trading fees can take a significant chunk out of your profit from investing. 10. Pay attention to how long you own the stock – There are tax benefits for owning a stock for more than a year. Take advantage of paying lower taxes on your gains! If you have losses and don’t want the stock anymore it may be beneficial to sell the stock if you own it for less than one year to get the higher tax rate benefit. 11. Be patient – I cannot stress this enough, you need to be patient with your investments. They will rise and fall in value but be patient and stick to your investment timeline. 12. Keep up to date – Know how the companies you invest in are doing. If they have a bad quarter because the world economy is under pressure you should know this. If they are under an investigation you may want to reassess your investment. Knowing the latest news with your investment is very important. 13. Use websites like Yahoo Finance or Google Finance – These websites will show you real time prices of the stocks, the latest news with the stocks, and give detailed statistics about everything you need to know about the company. They are great, FREE, resources that everybody should use. You can download the app on your phone and keep track of your stocks very easily. I personally use Yahoo Finance as it is very easy to use and has a wealth of information available.

**Don’t**

1. Buy small number of shares – The common rule is that your trading fees should be no more than 2% of your overall investment. Eg. If your broker charges you $5 to purchase stock, the minimum you should purchase $250 worth of stock. Small transactions all increase trading fees. 2. Wait – There is no correct time to enter the stock market so don’t wait for the “perfect time.” 3. Invest on emotion – Keeping your emotions separate from investing in stocks can be very difficult but is necessary. Make sure you are doing the adequate research when buying/selling a stock and not buying/selling because you like/dislike the company. 4. Do nothing – Doing nothing is probably the worst decision somebody can make. Doing nothing does not increase your wealth. Take the leap of faith and enter the investing world to grow your wealth. 5. Over invest – It is very important to know how much you can invest without affecting your financial situation. Setting a budget on how much you can invest is very important. If you are unsure how to budget check out my article which can help you figure out how much money you can invest on a monthly basis. 6. Listen to everything you hear – There will be many articles you read that say investing in this stock will guarantee you a return of --%. Don’t listen to many of these recommendations as they are normally false. No matter how credited the source may be, do your own research first! 7. Be greedy - Know when to sell your “winning” stocks and your “losing” stocks no matter how much you like them. Taking a loss on what you thought was a great investment can be very hard but it must be done to ensure you do not continue to lose money, should the stock continue to fall.

**What are some do’s and don’ts you can think of?** Can you think of any other do’s and don’ts of investing? If you enjoyed this article check out my website [www.themillennialbudget.com](www.themillennialbudget.com).com to see more.
